rawFindings.title: Methods incorrectly create new route instances each call causing duplicate registrations
rawFindings.explanation: In the methods forEach loop, the code changed from using this._router.route(path) to this._baseRoute(path) which maintains a cache of routes to avoid duplicates. Without this caching, calling app.VERB multiple times for the same path creates multiple separate route instances, leading to unexpected behavior in routing.
rawFindings.suggestion: Keep track of base routes by caching them keyed by path and always use the cached route instance when adding handlers for paths to avoid duplicate route registrations.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Calling app.get('/example', handler1) then app.get('/example', handler2) would create two handlers on different route instances, both matching '/example' separately, causing unexpected behavior.

rawFindings.title: Special-cased app.all() creates new route instance each call instead of reusing cached
rawFindings.explanation: In app.all, the new code calls this._baseRoute(path) which caches and reuses route instances properly. The previous code was calling this._router.route(path) directly, creating a new route instance each time and possibly causing multiple registrations and conflicts when app.all is used multiple times for the same path.
rawFindings.suggestion: Use a cached base route from this._baseRoute(path) inside app.all to prevent duplicate route creation and ensure that multiple app.all calls for the same path add handlers on the same route instance.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Multiple calls to app.all('/path', middleware) would register multiple route instances for '/path', leading to unexpected middleware run behaviors or conflicts.
